topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: The biological basis of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as clonal evolution driven by mutations whose consequences depend on cellular susceptibility and a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental contributions to cancer can be distinguished from inherited susceptibility and chance.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and host biology.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, with their effects depending on chemical reactivity and host metabolism.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent promoter activity before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain tissue and developmental susceptibility before placing that dependence on biological context within a recap of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogen exposure through mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how patterns in cancer genomes can provide evidence of previous exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods for assessing carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how carcinogenic potential can be investigated when controlled exposure experiments in humans are unethical.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as balances between risks and benefits.
